blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Brazil is seeking to expand its investments and economic cooperation with the Philippines in energy, defense, semiconductors and agriculture, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva saying the two countries must do more to expand bilateral trade. In an exclusive online interview with the Inquirer ahead of his state visit to Manila, Lula said bilateral trade had quadrupled over the past decade but remained far below its potential, considering the size of their respective economies. “The Philippines has 115 million people, while Brazil has 214 million.
